The one decision that makes this possible

You do not need fifteen weeks of material by September 7. You need Week 1 finished, the container built for the other fourteen, and a rhythm that keeps you two weeks ahead of the class. Thirty four topics in fifteen days is not a plan, it is how a term gets away from you in October.

Module 1 is three weeks and seven topics. That is the September 7 target. Weeks 2 and 3 give you a fortnight of runway from day one, and the two week buffer is what you defend for the rest of the term.

Priorities, in order

What to build, and what can wait

  1. Tier 1 · before Sep 7

    Module 1 teaching material, seven topics

    • Week 1, Foundations of Physiology, Quantitative Skills, Chemical Foundations
    • Week 2, Membrane Structure and Diffusion, Membrane Transport, Membrane Potential
    • Week 3, Cell Signaling
    • Each topic is one notes page, one concept video, one slide deck
    • Plus the syllabus, which does not exist yet and is the one thing a college will ask for
  2. Tier 1 · before Sep 7

    The container, built once, filled forever

    • A week hub template. Only week-01 exists. Build it as a generator that reads the schedule, the way the calendar does, and fourteen weeks appear for free
    • course-materials.html, the page four dock tiles already point at
    • Both are a day of work that saves a fortnight later
  3. Tier 2 · week 1 to 3 of term

    Stay two weeks ahead, and add the drawings

    • Module 2 topics, six of them, built while the class is inside Module 1
    • Weekly drawing prompt per week, off the checklists already written
    • The three review pages, chemistry, math and anatomy
    • The patient file project brief, which students start early and you want stable before they do
  4. Tier 3 · after the term opens

    The lab, and everything else

    • The lab manual is written and three labs are built. PhysioEx covers the gap while you finish your own, which is exactly what a fallback is for
    • Your own simulators replace PhysioEx one week at a time, in the week they are needed
    • Lab skills checklist, generated from the lab manual, which already carries what students should be able to do and what they hand in
    • Practice exams, brain dump prompts, Virtual Office, Study With Me
